catalog_quote: 0.0 In this section the probable phonemic systems of the Kwalean and Manubaran languages of Rigo are sketched and compared. These sketches are based on survey materials and need to be checked against more extensive material. ... Primary stress is marked ' before the stressed syllable. 1.0 The phonological systems of the Kwalean and Manubaran languages of Rigo are similar, notwithstanding quite wide variation across the more numerous dialects of the Manubaran languages. Each of the languages has sets of stops, fricatives, nasals, a vibrant or lateral (depending on interpretation), and at least five vowels. None of the languages is tonal but stress seems to be phonemic in each. Sequences of like vowels are either stressed on the second vowel or are separated by a glottal stop. ... audit.reasoning: (1) Quote verified verbatim on p. 916 of the held Dutton 1970 PDF (page image and text layer), Maria section on p. 917 as located. (2) The coding 'lexical' rests on a 1970 survey-based phoneme sketch whose author hedges the claim ('seems to be phonemic', 'need to be checked'); but per Glottolog 5.3 and Dutton 1975:636 (fetched sources now from sealang, no later description of Maria exists, so it is very probably the best available source and is held. (3) Nothing found contradicts the coding; the only stated regularity (like-vowel sequences stressed on the second vowel) is already in the record's prule. Wishlist is limited to sister-language Doromu-Koki grammars (family-level check) and an unverifiable SIL-PNG listing check; none is a Maria stress description. Hence 'thin' (old, hedged survey sketch, nothing better exists) with no ac

sources.quote: p. 636: 'Very little is known about the structure of the Manubaran languages, except for the notes I published in Dutton 1970, and nothing has been published in any of them.' p. 622 (all SE TNG languages, not Maria-specific): 'Some languages are tonal but stress is generally important and related to intonation which may be quite complex.' No Maria-specific stress rule.
